canonicalExplanation.summary: A **lambda** is an unnamed function object you write inline: `[capture](params) { body }`. The **capture list** decides how it sees surrounding variables. `[x]` **copies** x when the lambda is created, so later changes outside don't affect it. `[&x]` **refers** to x, so the lambda sees changes, but only while x **still exists**. `[=]` and `[&]` capture everything used, by copy or by reference. A lambda that **outlives** the variables it captured by reference (stored, returned, or run later on another thread) holds **dangling references**. Captured copies are `const` inside the lambda unless you mark it **`mutable`**.

sections.heading: Start here
sections.body:
A learner builds a filter `auto is_high = [&](int s) { return s >= threshold; };`, then changes threshold for a different report, and the first report's filter silently changes too. Another lambda returned from a function crashes when called. A count_if lambda captures threshold by value so later changes to the outer variable do not alter the predicate. In this lesson you'll implement and trace value and reference captures in an algorithm call.

```predict
{"question": "`int t = 50; auto f = [t](int s) { return s >= t; }; t = 90;` What is f(60)?", "options": ["false", "true: f copied t = 50 when it was created"], "answer": 1, "why": "Capture by value freezes the value at creation."}
```

sections.heading: Before you begin
sections.body: You should know **Iterators and invalidation**, **Overloading and default arguments**, **Standard algorithms** and **Value, reference and const-reference parameters**.

includes: Write lambdas for algorithms and choose value or reference captures deliberately.
Recognise dangling reference captures and use mutable for modifiable copies.

outcomes: Implement and trace value and reference captures in an algorithm call.

examples.title: A threshold captured by value
examples.situation: A count_if lambda captures threshold by value so later changes to the outer variable do not alter the predicate.
walkthrough: **A count_if lambda captures threshold by value:** [threshold](int s) { return s >= threshold; }.
**So later changes to the outer variable:** threshold = 90 for another report afterwards,
**Do not alter the predicate:** the stored filter will still count scores >= 70, giving 3.
examples.result: Each filter keeps the rule it was built with.

examples.title: The returned filter that crashed
examples.situation: make_filter returned [&threshold](int s) {...}. Calling the filter later reads freed stack memory.
walkthrough: threshold was a parameter: its lifetime ended when make_filter returned.
examples.result: The returned filter owns its own copy and works indefinitely.

misconceptions.mistakenBelief: A lambda using [&] safely keeps every referenced local alive for as long as the lambda object exists.
misconceptions.correction: Reference captures don't extend lifetimes. If the lambda outlives the captured variables, its references dangle; capture by value for lambdas that are stored or returned.
misconceptions.diagnosticPrompt: In "The returned filter that crashed", why did the reference dangle?

analogy.example: Capturing by value is **taking a photo** of a whiteboard: later edits to the board don't change your photo. Capturing by reference is **remembering which room the board is in**: you always see the latest version, until the room is demolished (scope ends).
limitations: Photos are cheap for small things; copying big objects isn't.
mutable lets you draw on your own photo.

nearTransfer.prompt: Predict and check: a lambda capturing x by value and one by reference, both created when x = 1, called after x = 5. Then write a mutable lambda that counts its own calls.

farTransfer.prompt: Write make_multiplier(int factor) returning a std::function<int(int)>, and a vector of such functions. Show a buggy version with [&factor] under -fsanitize=address, then fix it and test all multipliers.
scaffold: Sanitizer reports stack-use-after-return (may need an option).

remediation.explanation: For each capture ask: **will this lambda run after the variable's scope ends?** If yes, or if it shouldn't see later changes, capture by value.
remediation.retryPrompt: Apply this to "The returned filter that crashed".

recap.summary: To write lambdas safely, capture by value when the lambda should keep a snapshot or may outlive the current scope, capture by reference only when it must see or update a variable that will outlive it, mark lambdas mutable to change their own copies, and use them to express predicates for algorithms.
